posts.title_en: Poultry Processor Achieves Zero Bone Complaints [TEST]
posts.excerpt_en: How a large poultry producer eliminated bone fragment complaints with LITUBO X-ray systems. [TEST DATA]
posts.body_en:
Challenge

A European poultry processor was receiving customer complaints about bone fragments in boneless chicken fillets.

Solution

LITUBO LX-5000 X-ray inspection systems installed at the end-of-line with real-time rejection and automatic reporting.

Results

Zero bone fragment complaints in 18 months post-installation.

posts.title_en: Can X-rays penetrate all packaging types? [TEST]
posts.excerpt_en: FAQ about X-ray penetration through various packaging materials. [TEST DATA]
posts.body_en: Yes. X-ray inspection is effective through metal cans, foil pouches, glass jars, plastic trays and cardboard boxes. The X-ray beam penetrates the packaging and the product; only dense foreign bodies are flagged.

posts.title_en: Why is metal detection harder with wet or conductive products? [TEST]
posts.excerpt_en: FAQ: product effect on metal detector performance. [TEST DATA]
posts.body_en: High-moisture and high-salt products conduct electricity and can mimic a metal signal. Modern metal detectors use multi-frequency technology to separate the product effect from genuine metal contamination, maintaining sensitivity without false rejects.

posts.title_en: How often should inspection systems be calibrated? [TEST]
posts.excerpt_en: FAQ: recommended calibration intervals for LITUBO inspection systems. [TEST DATA]
posts.body_en: LITUBO recommends daily performance verification using certified test pieces at the start of each production shift. Full calibration should be performed by a certified technician at least once per year, or after any major maintenance.

posts.author: LITUBO Applications Team
posts.title_en: Metal Detector Sensitivity: A Technical Guide [TEST]
posts.excerpt_en: Understanding sensitivity parameters to match your metal detector to your product and packaging requirements. [TEST DATA]
posts.body_en:
Sensitivity Factors

Metal detector sensitivity depends on aperture size, operating frequency, product effect, and environmental conditions.

  • Ferrous metals: easiest to detect
  • Non-ferrous metals: moderate sensitivity
  • Stainless steel: most challenging

posts.author: LITUBO Editorial
posts.excerpt_en: A concise overview of how X-ray inspection protects food products from physical contaminants. [TEST DATA - DO NOT PUBLISH]
posts.body_en:
Introduction

X-ray inspection systems detect dense foreign bodies such as metal, glass, stone and bone in packaged and bulk food products.

How It Works

A focused X-ray beam passes through the product. Dense objects absorb more radiation and appear as darker areas on the image, which are flagged by the system automatically.

products_files.caption_en: Full machine photo — LT-180C free-fall metal detector

product_sections.body_en: Product material enters the machine from the top hopper and falls freely through the cylindrical detection coil. The coil generates a balanced electromagnetic field; when a ferrous or non-ferrous metal particle disrupts this field, the detector triggers an alarm and activates the pneumatic rejection valve. The separation flap opens momentarily to divert the contaminated stream to the waste bin, then closes to return the machine to normal operation. The system operates continuously with no moving parts in the product flow path during normal inspection.

product_section_items.body_en: No belt drive or mechanical feeder required; product flows under gravity through the detection head.
AirTac GFR200-08 filter regulator drives a fast-acting separation flap for reliable metal ejection.
Sealed electronics cabinet withstands washdown and dusty environments.
All product-contact surfaces are stainless steel for food-safety compliance.
Integrated controller with LED status indicators (Power, Running, Detection, Valve, Alarm), menu navigation, and key-switch lockout.
Hygienic tri-clamp fittings at inlet and outlet for easy cleaning and pipeline integration.
